claims.statement: A house at Pompeii was converted into a fullery, where workers washed clothes and processed cloth. Vats occupied the former domestic spaces, and a terrace was used for drying. The archaeological park describes most of the workforce as enslaved. The building connects household architecture with demanding commercial labour.

Washing clothes at Pompeii: 79 CE to 79 CE. Snapshot of evidence preserved by the 79 CE eruption, not a one-year business or its opening date. Stephanus’s ownership is inferred from inscriptions; the identity of a body found at the entrance is not assumed. Map point locates Pompeii, not the individual workshop.
UNESCO Pompeii city-site reference; not a shop coordinate or volcanic vent.
